literal: Among Taizu's three marks of imperial stature: he replaced the Yaolian and honored the nine accounts above his own camp—first;

idiomatic: He destroyed Bohai but kept its clan registers subordinate to the Yaolian—second;

literal: He absorbed the Xi king's people and soothed their account tribes, ranking them like the state clan—third.

literal: Three marks of heroic wisdom: employing the imperial maternal uncles to pair with the imperial clan, elevating the Yishi to balance the Xi king, and setting Two Courts to control the Yaolian—that is enough.

literal: Taizu received the throne from the Yaolian and placed the nine accounts above the one imperial clan account, establishing the Changgun Office to serve them while regular offices did not interfere.
